title: The similarity characterization for products of two involutions
statement:
Let $V$ be an infinite-dimensional vector space, and let $u\in\operatorname{GL}(V)$. An **involution** is an invertible endomorphism whose square is the identity, and two endomorphisms are **similar** if they are conjugate by a vector-space isomorphism.

**Involution-product conjecture.** The endomorphism $u$ is the product of two involutions in $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ if and only if $u$ is similar to its inverse.

This conjecture extends the finite-dimensional theorem characterizing products of two involutions by similarity to the inverse. The infinite-dimensional setting has no invariant-factor criterion, so the validity of this equivalence remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.04273

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).
source_name: Clément de Seguins Pazzis, “Sums and products of two quadratic endomorphisms of a countable-dimensional vector space”, arXiv:2107.04273 (2021).
